Revised assessment incorporating the Financial Stability Report: The FOMC statement is moderately positive with a mild hawkish bias—highlighting strong labor markets, robust household spending, and inflation near 2%, while acknowledging softer business fixed investment and “roughly balanced” risks. The November 2018 Financial Stability Report tempers this tone: it flagged elevated asset valuations, rising nonfinancial business leverage (especially in riskier credit), and some underwriting weakness in leveraged lending, even as funding risks remained low and bank capital/liquidity strong. These stability considerations support cautious normalization (as reflected in “some further gradual increases” and continued balance-sheet runoff) rather than aggressive tightening, nudging the overall tone slightly less positive than a pure macro read would suggest.
